keeps.name: Greene-Sullivan State Forest - Narrow Lake Campground
keeps.waterfront_evidence: Camp.IN.gov per-site records flag P1 and P2 'Proximity to Water: Lakefront' (GIS 39.03414,-87.25939 and 39.03391,-87.25947); satellite at 39.0340,-87.2591 (0.29 m/px): their small gravel loop has open ground ~14 m to the reed fringe and ~33 m to open water, no road on the lake side; Dyrt photo from a trailer at P2 (Sep 2021 review) shows gravel, grass, then the lake. DNR gives Narrow 9 acres. 3DEP: pads 160.7 m, pool 157.6 m, an easy slope. P3-P5 carry no water flag and sit along the road ~100+ m south of the lake. The grey-roofed units on the spur north of the old pin are rent-a-camp cabins (C15-C17 by GIS), not RVs. Overpass down; distances from imagery.
keeps.inclusion_evidence: Camp.IN.gov sells sites P1-P5 of 'Greene Sullivan Narrow Campground' as site type Electric, access Drive-In, category 'RV Site'; no equipment length is posted and the DNR page is silent on length. A Sep 2021 Dyrt reviewer stayed at P1 in a travel trailer of unstated length and found P1-P3 unlevel. Photo of a P-site shows a wide gravel spur. Pad length unclear, so kept with a caveat.
keeps.note: On the south side of Narrow Lake, among the rent-a-camp cabins. Sites P1 and P2 are on a small loop near the lake's west end, beside SR 159 behind a board fence; P3-P5 are along the campground road to the east, back from the water. The agency gives no length. A 2021 Dyrt reviewer in a travel trailer found P1-P3 unlevel and the highway noisy. --Claude

sites.note: Camp.IN.gov's five sites sold for camping here, P1-P5, listed as Electric with no amperage or length posted. DNR's combined 100 ('family campsites of Narrow Lake, Wampler Lake, and Reservoir #26') gives no split; no other RV site was identified here, and every other structure with a GIS point is a cabin or shelter.

facilities.note: Pit toilets; drinking water is seasonal. Table, fire ring and grill at each site. The forest's dump station is here.

season.note: Camp.IN.gov status for the forest; DNR calls the drinking water seasonal.

booking.note: Sites P1-P5 are booked by site on Camp.IN.gov. DNR's page also describes first-come camping at all three campgrounds; whether Narrow Lake has any first-come sites isn't stated.

fees.note: Camp.IN.gov lists Electric at $33-$43 a night. DNR's statewide reservation table names Greene-Sullivan '(some campsites)', with $33, $40 and $43 as the low ends for Sun-Wed, Thu-Sat and holiday weekends.

adds.name: Greene-Sullivan State Forest - Reservoir 26 Campground
adds.waterfront_evidence: Satellite at 39.0180,-87.2422 (0.29 m/px): west pads ~40 m from the 42-acre reservoir (DNR), across a levee with a track on it. USGS 3DEP transect at 39.0181: pool 153.8 m, crest 154.6 m, toe 149.9 m, pads ~151.4 m, so pads sit ~2.4 m below pool behind a ~3 m berm: no lake value. Overpass down; distances from imagery.
adds.inclusion_evidence: DNR names it as one of three family campgrounds, with a wheelchair-accessible site, pit toilets and a playground; length not stated. A loop with gravel spurs and parked units shows on imagery. May 2020 Dyrt review: 'Reservoir 26 is open and flat (good for larger RVs)'; another 2020 review warns of Wampler and Reservoir 26: 'most of these sites are not conducive to larger campers'. Pad length unclear, so kept with a caveat.
adds.note: A loop off W 25 N with its own two driveways, in the south-central forest, behind the levee on the east side of Reservoir 26. Fishing pier and a trail around the reservoir. The agency gives no length; 2020 Dyrt reviewers disagree, one calling it open and flat and good for larger RVs, another warning most sites here and at Wampler don't suit larger campers. --Claude

sites.note: DNR publishes only a combined figure ('each of the 100 family campsites of Narrow Lake, Wampler Lake, and Reservoir #26') and no split, so this campground has no count of its own.

facilities.note: Pit toilets; drinking water is seasonal. A picnic table and grill at each site. Playground, a wheelchair-accessible site and a wheelchair-accessible fishing pier. The forest's dump station is at Narrow Lake (camper report).

booking.note: Self check-in station in the campground or at the forest office.

fees.note: $12.15 a night: the Indiana DNR's first-come, first-served primitive rate for state forest campgrounds.

adds.name: Greene-Sullivan State Forest - Wampler Lake Campground
adds.waterfront_evidence: Located and pinned: satellite at 39.0175,-87.2200 (0.29 m/px) shows the signed campground off the causeway road, entrance ~39.0182,-87.2197, with white units parked on open grass at 39.01781,-87.21879, ~11-20 m from an arm of Wampler Lake, no road between. Same 147.2 m pool on USGS 3DEP (unit 148.7 m); DNR gives the lake 80 acres. Dated firsthand photo, Dyrt 'Wampler Lake Campsite' (2020 review): gravel pad beside the water. Overpass down; distances from imagery.
adds.inclusion_evidence: DNR names it as one of three family campgrounds, length not stated. May 2020 Dyrt review: 'Wampler lake is not as open but RVs can get into some of the sites'; another 2020 review warns 'most of these sites are not conducive to larger campers and the gravel access roads are sometimes washboard'. Imagery shows RV-sized units roughly 6-9 m long at 39.01754,-87.21986, 39.01781,-87.21879, 39.01807,-87.21946 and 39.01574,-87.22008. Site sign and check-in station photographed 2020. Pad length unclear, so kept with a caveat.
adds.note: On the wooded fingers of Wampler Lake at the east side of the forest, off the road across the lake's causeway from N 1500 W. Some sites sit at the water. The agency gives no length; 2020 Dyrt reviewers say RVs can get into some sites, that most don't suit larger campers and that the gravel roads can be washboard. Scout before pulling in. --Claude
